scope: THE CONNECTION STATE MACHINE: status is a mapping of [netobj+0xC8] and two flags; status 2 (which selects ui_state 5) is reached by two different paths

the_function_0xba0780.0xBA078D: je 0xBA079F  - flag 0x644 == 0 takes the second path
the_function_0xba0780.0xBA078F: path A: if [0xC8] == 2 or [0xC8] == 1 -> return 2; otherwise return [0xC8]
the_function_0xba0780.0xBA07A4: path B with [0xC8] == 2: eax = 0; if [0x5E8] == 3 then eax = 1; then eax += 1
the_function_0xba0780.result: path B returns 1 when [0x5E8] == 3, and 2 otherwise

how_status_2_is_reached: we measured status 2, so one of those holds
what_would_leave_ui_state_5: the ui-5 branch at 0x8037D6 is taken when the mapped status equals 2
so the client leaves that screen when the status becomes anything else
concretely: either [0xC8] moves out of {1,2} (path A) or out of {2} (path B), or [0x5E8] becomes 3 while [0xC8] stays 2 (path B returns 1)
so [0x5E8] == 3 is the most specific single condition that would flip the screen
what_0x5e8_likely_is: a sub-state of the connection: in this protocol family the client distinguishes between being connected to the server and having the session/server-browser handshake finished
[0x5E8] == 3 would then mean the deeper handshake completed, which is exactly the layer that net_state 10 does not cover
the_next_measurement_if_work_continues: read [netobj+0x644], [netobj+0xC8] and [netobj+0x5E8] directly in the live client
those three values pin down which path is taken and therefore which one has to move
